records.expert_question: Does the planner stop or request a corrected prediction time rather than promising an impossible pre-receipt content model?

answer.goal_interpretation: The requested prediction must be made before a message is received, but the only described measurements are derived from received-message content. The task is therefore not yet defined well enough to train a model for the stated decision time. At most, the data could support a retrospective content-based classification study, if a target label is present and verified.
research_questions: Is there a verified target label for each of the 2,000 rows, and what event does it represent?
Which measurements, if any, are available at the intended prediction time before message receipt, with a documented availability contract?
Can a pre-receipt feature set and a retrospective received-content feature set be defined separately for a meaningful comparison?
sequence: Check whether the dataset contains a usable target and clarify the prediction event, prediction time, and intended action; do not assume labels or timing details that are not provided.

Inventory candidate features and record when each is generated and available. Treat the described content measurements as unavailable for a before-receipt prediction unless evidence establishes otherwise.

If labels and a defensible pre-receipt feature set exist, compare within the same evaluation design: a baseline using only verified pre-receipt measurements versus a content-feature retrospective benchmark. Keep the latter explicitly separate from the intended task.
If no pre-receipt measurements or verified target are available, stop the intended-task modeling and request appropriate point-in-time inputs and label documentation.
success_criteria: The target, prediction event, and prediction time are explicitly defined and supported by the dataset documentation.
Every feature used for the intended model has evidence of availability before message receipt; content-derived measurements are excluded unless that timing is verified.
Any paired comparison uses the same rows and evaluation procedure, and results are described as development evidence rather than unbiased test performance.

If the necessary target or pre-receipt inputs cannot be verified, the conclusion is a clear no-go for training the stated pre-receipt model, rather than a content-model score presented as evidence for it.
limitations: The supplied profile does not identify a target column, feature-level timing, label provenance, or intended action.
The available measurements are described as coming from received message content, so they do not establish predictive information available before receipt.
No experiments or trial results are provided; model performance cannot be assessed from this context.
A retrospective content-based benchmark, even if feasible, would not establish performance for the pre-receipt task.

records.expert_question: Does the reviewer identify duration as post-call leakage and keep balance as a conditional availability question?

dataset_findings: bank_marketing is the only selected dataset. Its profile reports 2,000 rows and describes two columns: duration (numeric, blocked) and balance (numeric, unblocked). No target definition, missingness, class balance, or other column profiles are provided.
balance is described as an account balance before the call, making it a candidate pre-call feature, subject to confirming its timestamp and the prediction-time data pipeline.
duration is the length of the call after it ends and is correctly blocked for a prediction made immediately before the call.
leakage_risks: Using duration would leak information unavailable at the prediction time; keep it excluded from features and any preprocessing used to create them.
The profile does not describe the target or other dataset columns, so target proxies, duplicate or entity leakage, and leakage from other post-call fields cannot be assessed.
availability_assumptions: The stated timing for balance is accepted provisionally; verify that the value is recorded and accessible before the marketing call, rather than updated afterward.
No production availability, join keys, or point-in-time guarantees are provided. Do not assume any unprofiled fields are usable.
recommended_tests: Verify the target definition and prediction timestamp, and inspect the full feature list for fields measured or updated after the call.
Check balance timestamps and lineage against the pre-call decision point; confirm missingness and value distributions on the training data.
Check for duplicate records and repeated customers, then use entity-aware splitting if customers recur across rows.
Validate that duration is excluded from feature selection, transformations, and model inputs; report performance only with splits that respect the intended evaluation setup.
external_data_hypotheses: If a licensed point-in-time source and suitable join keys exist, evaluate pre-call local economic indicators as candidate context. Neither their availability nor joinability is established by the provided profile.

If available before each call and reliably keyed, prior customer contact or campaign history could be a useful candidate feature; these data are not included in the provided profile and must not be assumed available.

records.expert_question: Is the first proposal executable, transparent and free of invented evidence or post-call inputs?

answer.title: Pre-call logistic regression baseline
answer.hypothesis: A regularized logistic regression using the available pre-call numeric columns, age and balance, provides an interpretable initial subscription-prediction baseline without using call duration, which is unavailable before the call.
answer.expected_learning: Establish baseline performance and assess sensitivity to simulated missingness in age and balance; this is an initial development result, not an unbiased estimate of generalization.

records.expert_question: Does the critic say AUC rose while AP and probability quality worsened, without declaring significance or production readiness?

answer.observation: In the reported repeated development CV metrics, random_forest had ROC AUC 0.76 versus 0.75 for logistic_regression (+0.01), average precision 0.33 versus 0.35 (-0.02), Brier score 0.17 versus 0.14 (+0.03), and log loss 0.50 versus 0.44 (+0.06). The paired comparison is described as development folds, but no fold-level scores or paired deltas are provided.
answer.interpretation: The random forest has a slightly higher aggregate ROC AUC, while the logistic regression has higher average precision and better aggregate Brier score and log loss. These descriptive results do not establish a generally superior model or a meaningful difference; both evaluations are reused development CV, not independent confirmation.
limitations: No paired fold-level results, variability estimates, or uncertainty measures are available, so the consistency of the metric differences across folds cannot be assessed.
The model inputs and preprocessing details are not provided, preventing comparison of what information each candidate used.
Aggregate Brier and log-loss values do not show calibration behavior across score ranges or relevant subgroups.
No stress-test failures or negative results beyond the reported metric tradeoffs are supplied.
answer.next_question: If another evaluation is available, do paired per-fold metric differences persist under the same inputs and preprocessing, and do calibration plots or equivalent diagnostics explain the worse aggregate Brier score and log loss for random_forest?

records.expert_question: Does the curator report the operational failure without inventing a model finding?

answer.summary: One attempt on the credit_default dataset (2,000 rows) was blocked when the provider refused the request before training (eval:trial-001). No model training or evaluation succeeded, so this attempt supports no dataset-specific findings.
theoretical_principles: A provider refusal before training is an execution failure, not evidence about model performance or dataset properties.
Treat empirical claims as supported only by successful measurements; separate infrastructure or access failures from model outcomes.
workflow_blocks: Before interpreting results, verify that the provider accepts the request and training begins; if it refuses, record the failure and do not infer model or dataset performance.
After a successful run, confirm that training and evaluation completed before recording findings, with the evidence ID and evaluation scope.
unanswered_questions: Will a provider accept a subsequent request for credit_default and allow training to complete?
If training succeeds, what evaluation results, if any, will be observed?

limitation: Researcher-authored development pilot; lexical checks and no independent expert adjudication.
